# Factory · AI Teammate leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agents factory pack, top-level: GitHub requires reusable workflows at the .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# The dev→review→rework machine loop for GitHub-issues trackers, hosted in
# dmtools-agents so target repositories carry only a thin stub (event
# triggers + this call) plus .dmtools/config.js, secrets and vars. Runs in
# the CALLER's context: github.repository = the target repo; vars.* and
# secrets.* resolve from the caller (each target pins its own versions).
#
# Legs (guard derives the slot when `leg` is empty):
#   bug | story | review | rework — the runner configs live in the TARGET repo
#   (.dmtools/runners/*), wired via .dmtools/config.js sm.runners.
#
# Loop mechanics (identical to the dmtools-dart template this was ported
# from — see that file's history for the full rationale):
#   issue assigned/labeled → guard → ticket input → dmtools run <runner>
#   → agent develops → PR ("Closes #NN") → review verdict step:
#       APPROVE + green PR checks → pr_approved → merge (merge-trigger/stub)
#       CHANGES_REQUESTED        → agent:rework (bounded: MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS,
#                                  then needs-human escalation)
#   Review/rework queue labels are stripped at cycle end (no self-loops).
#   fa sessions ride the fa-sess/gh-<n> branch (cache saves are denied on
#   issues-event runs); fa project memory is committed back to the repo.
#
# Secrets (via `secrets: inherit`): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT — labels added
#   with GITHUB_TOKEN never fire `labeled` events; pushes must not author
#   as github-actions[bot]), ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY.
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
#   MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS (default 2).
#
# Caller stub:
#   on:
#     issues: {types: [assigned, labeled]}
#     workflow_dispatch: {inputs: {issue: {type: number}, leg: {type: string}}}
#   concurrency:
#     group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue }}
#     cancel-in-progress: false
#   jobs:
#     factory:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue }}
#         leg: ${{ inputs.leg || '' }}
#         reason: ${{ inputs.reason || 'stub' }}
#       secrets: inherit

name: 'Factory · AI Teammate'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label (self-hosted pools must be visible to the CALLING org)'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (string: number-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions). Empty when pr is given (PR-anchored run, #687).'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687). Exactly one of issue|pr must be set.'
        required: false
        type: string
      machine-author:
        description: "Deployment's machine (bot) login (#687): gates rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews (auto-approve via pr_approved is author-agnostic per the owner rule). Injected as jobParams.machineAuthor — branch-independent (the checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config)."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: "Which leg to run: dev | review | rework (empty = derive from labels/assignees)"
        required: false
        type: string
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      factory_ref:
        description: 'The dmtools-agents ref the factory runs from (the literal in the stub uses-line). github.workflow_ref cannot serve: in a called workflow it carries the CALLER ref, not the uses-ref.'
        required: true
        type: string
      flutter-version:
        description: 'Flutter SDK for agent work (cached). "" skips — for pure-Dart targets that only need dart from the runner image. A value installs Flutter+matching Dart via flutter-action with SDK caching (e.g. "stable", "3.38.0").'
        required: false
        default: 'stable'
        type: string

    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:
        description: 'PAT with repo scope — machine labels, pushes, PR/issue API (secrets: inherit does not cross repository boundaries).'
        required: true
      ZAI_CODE_KEY:
        description: 'z.ai API key (dev/rework provider + review queue fallback)'
        required: false
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY:
        description: 'kimi API key (review provider, first in the queue)'
        required: false

# NOTE: no `concurrency` here — the caller stub owns the per-issue group.
# A reusable workflow with the SAME group as its caller deadlocks: the caller
# holds the group while the called workflow waits for it forever (pending, 0 jobs).

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  # actions/cache@v6 save phase needs actions:write on github.token.
  actions: write

jobs:
  guard:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}
      config: ${{ steps.check.outputs.config }}
      kind: ${{ steps.check.outputs.kind }}
      anchor: ${{ steps.check.outputs.anchor }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout target repository (config, runners)
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # caller-repo checkout: the factory reads .dmtools/config.js from
          # the TARGET repository, never from the factory pack
          ref: ${{ github.ref }}
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Decide whether this event is for the agent
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ inputs.pr }}
          # Event context rides through from the caller (issues events) —
          # empty for pure dispatches. The guard ALWAYS refreshes from the
          # API (queued runs see a stale payload); this is only a fallback.
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ join(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, ' ') }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
          ACTOR: ${{ github.event.action || github.event_name }}
          # #544: the `labeled` event sender — the owner-override gate checks
          # its repo permission before honoring a manual agent:rework.
          # Empty for schedule-scan dispatches (SM ticks): the label is
          # trusted as-is there (see rework_override_ok below).
          SENDER: ${{ github.event.sender.login || '' }}
          INPUT_LEG: ${{ inputs.leg }}
          INPUT_REASON: ${{ inputs.reason }}
          # The assignee gate below compares against the machine login.
          # AGENT_HANDLE lives on the TEAMMATE job's env — without it here
          # the guard's $AGENT_HANDLE is empty, `grep -w` never matches, and
          # assignment-triggered dev legs never start (live: dmtools-dart
          # run 35519287617 — issue #173 assigned to ai-teammate → skipped).
          AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
        run: |
          # Anchor validation (#687): exactly one of issue|pr.
          if [ -n "$NUMBER" ] && [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
            echo "::error::both issue ($NUMBER) and pr ($PR_NUMBER) given — exactly one anchor allowed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "$NUMBER" ] && [ -z "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
            echo "::error::no anchor — pass either issue or pr"
            exit 1
          fi

          # ── runners come from the TARGET repo (.dmtools/config.js) ──
          # The factory ships no repo-specific runners: sm.runners maps
          # legs to configs in this repository (see the integration guide,
          # "Overriding agents per repository"). dev covers bug and story.
          if [ ! -f .dmtools/config.js ]; then
            echo "::error::.dmtools/config.js not found — the factory needs sm.runners to know this repo's agents (docs/machine-factory-integration.md §5a)"
            exit 1
          fi
          ovr="$(node -e "try{const c=require('./.dmtools/config.js');const r=(c.sm&&c.sm.runners)||{};console.log([r.bug||r.dev||'',r.story||r.dev||'',r.review||'',r.rework||''].join('\t'))}catch(e){}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if [ -z "$ovr" ]; then
            echo "::error::sm.runners missing in .dmtools/config.js (bug/story[/dev], review, rework → runner config paths)"
            exit 1
          fi
          RUNNER_BUG="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f1)"
          RUNNER_STORY="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f2)"
          RUNNER_REVIEW="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f3)"
          RUNNER_REWORK="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f4)"
          echo "→ runners (from .dmtools/config.js): bug=${RUNNER_BUG:--} story=${RUNNER_STORY:--} review=${RUNNER_REVIEW:--} rework=${RUNNER_REWORK:--}"

          # Owner override gate (#544 owner rule, issue comment 3): a MANUAL
          # agent:rework label IS the explicit override — it fires rework on
          # ANY PR (machine or guest, with or without a local issue). But the
          # machine NEVER self-triggers rework on guest PRs, and a random
          # external labeler must not burn factory tokens. Where the
          # `labeled` event sender is known, gate the override on its repo
          # permission (write/admin/maintain). Schedule-scan dispatches and
          # non-labeled events carry no meaningful actor — the label is
          # trusted as-is (the SM consumed/verified it upstream).
          rework_override_ok() {
            if [ "$ACTOR" != "labeled" ] || [ -z "$SENDER" ]; then
              return 0
            fi
            perm="$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/collaborators/$SENDER/permission" -q .permission 2>/dev/null || true)"
            case "$perm" in
              admin|maintain|write) return 0 ;;
              *)
                echo "::warning::agent:rework by '$SENDER' (permission: ${perm:-none}) — the owner override requires write/admin; skipping (never fails the cycle, #544)"
                return 1
                ;;
            esac
          }

          # ── PR-anchored dispatch (#687): the PR is the anchor. Review was
          # the only leg defined for it — #544 extends the branch to REWORK:
          # a labeled PR with no resolvable LOCAL issue anchors on the PR
          # itself (pr-<N>, owner rule 3) and the rework runner derives its
          # context from the PR (review findings, failing checks).
          if [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
            state="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if [ -z "$state" ]; then
              # #544 rule 2: an unresolvable anchor is a warn-and-skip —
              # never exit 1. One bad number must not stall the machine loop.
              echo "::warning::PR #$PR_NUMBER could not be resolved in $GITHUB_REPOSITORY — skipping (clean no-op, #544)"
              echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
            fi
            if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
              echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER is ${state} — not for the agent"
              exit 0
            fi
            # 'blocked' = human hold (fa #939): the freeze switch applies to
            # PR-anchored legs too — a frozen PR gets no review/rework run.
            pr_blocked="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
              --json labels -q '([.labels[].name] | index("blocked")) != null' 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
            if [ "$pr_blocked" = "true" ]; then
              echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER carries blocked — human hold, the machine skips it entirely"
              exit 0
            fi
            leg="$INPUT_LEG"
            if [ -z "$leg" ] && echo "$INPUT_REASON" | grep -qi 'rework'; then
              leg="rework"
            fi
            if [ "$leg" = "rework" ]; then
              if ! rework_override_ok; then
                echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                exit 0
              fi
              echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "runner=$RUNNER_REWORK" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "config=factory-agents/pr_rework.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "kind=rework" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "→ PR-anchored REWORK of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>}, #544)"
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "runner=$RUNNER_REVIEW" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "config=factory-agents/pr_review.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "kind=review" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "→ PR-anchored review of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>})"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "anchor=gh-${NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          # ALWAYS refresh labels/assignees from the API — not just for
          # explicit dispatches. Event-triggered runs (issues:assigned,
          # labeled, ...) sit QUEUED behind the per-issue concurrency group,
          # and the github.event.issue payload they carry is a snapshot from
          # trigger time: a guard that trusts it misses labels the
          # already-running leg has since applied (status:In Development,
          # status:In Rework) and dispatches a duplicate dev/rework leg on
          # top of the live one (live: dmtools-dart run 36252718919 for #257;
          # a duplicate rework dispatch for #259). The event payload is only
          # a fallback when the API read itself fails.
          if fresh_labels="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')" \
            && fresh_assignees="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"; then
            LABELS="$fresh_labels"
            ASSIGNEES="$fresh_assignees"
          else
            echo "::warning::labels/assignees refresh failed for #$NUMBER — falling back to the (possibly stale) event payload"
          fi
          if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
            echo "→ dispatch: leg=$INPUT_LEG reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>}"
          fi
          # Closed issues are terminal: no agent runs on them. #544 rule 2:
          # a FAILED resolution (404 — missing issue or cross-repo ref like
          # 'dm.ai #601') is a warn-and-skip, never exit 1 — one bad anchor
          # must not turn the whole SM cycle red every 15 min.
          state="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if [ -z "$state" ]; then
            echo "::warning::issue #$NUMBER could not be resolved in $GITHUB_REPOSITORY (missing or cross-repo ref) — skipping this leg (clean no-op, #544)"
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "→ issue #$NUMBER is ${state} — not for the agent"
            exit 0
          fi
          # agent:skip — hard opt-out for smoke/verification tickets.
          if echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:skip"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "→ issue #$NUMBER carries agent:skip — agent bypassed"
            exit 0
          fi
          # 'blocked' = human hold (fa #939): the official freeze switch —
          # no leg starts on a frozen item, whatever the event (assignment,
          # any label echo). Same label the SM engine and the machine-SM
          # reconciler honor; removing it returns the item to the loop.
          if echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "blocked"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "→ issue #$NUMBER carries blocked — human hold, the machine skips it entirely"
            exit 0
          fi
          runner=""
          slot=""
          if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
            case "$INPUT_LEG" in
              rework) runner="$RUNNER_REWORK"; slot="rework" ;;
              review) runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW"; slot="review" ;;
              dev)
                title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
                if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' \
                  || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
                  runner="$RUNNER_BUG"; slot="bug"
                else
                  runner="$RUNNER_STORY"; slot="story"
                fi
                ;;
            esac
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:rework" \
            && ! echo "$LABELS" | grep -q 'status:In Rework'; then
            # status:In Rework = a rework leg already runs/ran — its own
            # status transition echoes back as a `labeled` event and would
            # re-derive the same leg on top of itself.
            # #544: manual agent:rework is the owner override — it fires
            # rework even from a `labeled` event, but only when the labeler
            # has write/admin (see rework_override_ok). Without permission
            # the override is ignored (runner stays empty → clean skip).
            if rework_override_ok; then
              runner="$RUNNER_REWORK"
            fi
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:review"; then
            # status:In Review is NOT an in-flight marker here — the DEV leg
            # sets it as the "ready for review" invitation, so blocking on it
            # kills the label-echo review trigger (live: dmtools-dart gh-182).
            # Real duplicate protection is the per-issue concurrency group.
            runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW"; slot="review"
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qE 'status:In Development|status:In Review|status:In Rework|in progress|ai_developed|ai_pr_reviewed|_wip|rework-round-'; then
            # Dev is a FRESH handoff only: once the loop has touched the
            # issue, later `labeled` events (the dev leg's OWN status:In
            # Development transition, SM backfill labels, ...) would
            # re-derive dev and queue a duplicate leg on top of the
            # running/finished one (live: fa gh-746 — the assigned-handoff
            # dev ran while its status-label echo queued a second dev).
            # The SM owns the loop from there; explicit dispatches
            # (inputs.leg) bypass this derive branch entirely.
            :
          elif echo "$ASSIGNEES" | grep -qw "$AGENT_HANDLE" \
            || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:dev"; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' \
              || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"; slot="bug"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"; slot="story"
            fi
          fi
          if [ -n "$runner" ]; then
            # Parent agent config — fa-session.sh derives the session group
            # from its basename (dev-write vs dev-review).
            # Parent pipeline by SLOT — custom runners (config overrides)
            # inherit the leg's pipeline, so a repo can swap the agent
            # without losing session/verdict semantics.
            case "$slot" in
              bug)     config="factory-agents/bug_development.json"; kind="dev" ;;
              story)   config="factory-agents/story_development.json"; kind="dev" ;;
              review)  config="factory-agents/pr_review.json";        kind="review" ;;
              rework)  config="factory-agents/pr_rework.json";        kind="dev" ;;
              *)       config="factory-agents/story_development.json"; kind="dev" ;;
            esac
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "runner=$runner" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "config=$config" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "kind=$kind" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "→ agent run: $runner (event=$ACTOR, labels=$LABELS, assignees=$ASSIGNEES)"
          else
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "→ not for the agent (event=$ACTOR, labels=$LABELS, assignees=$ASSIGNEES)"
          fi

  teammate:
    needs: guard
    if: needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    # A real fix is a 40-80 minute agent session (gh-623 burned a full RCA +
    # TDD cycle at exactly 61 minutes and the job was killed mid-work); dev
    # legs over Flutter sources run the analyzer + full flutter test suite
    # and live 2-3 hours (fa gh-1077 leg was killed mid-work at exactly 110
    # on 2026-09-30). The autocommit timer (300s) bounds the blast radius of
    # a kill; this timeout bounds the bill.
    timeout-minutes: 260
    # Workflow-level env is NOT supported in reusable (workflow_call)
    # workflows — the factory failed validation at startup until this
    # moved down to the job.
    env:
      AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
      FA_VERSION: ${{ vars.FA_VERSION_MACHINE || vars.FA_VERSION || 'latest' }}
      DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.14' }}
      MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS: ${{ vars.MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS || 2 }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout target repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # The engine rides factory-agents/ (checked out next), but the
          # parent runner configs reference the target's submodule paths
          # verbatim (agents/js/*.js, ./agents/scripts/*) so the machine
          # runs identically locally and in the factory — the submodule
          # MUST be initialized at the reviewed, pinned SHA.
          submodules: true
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Resolve factory ref (self-pin)
        # github.workflow_ref = "<owner>/<repo>/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@<ref>"
        # — runners, scripts and workflow are checked out at EXACTLY the ref
        # the caller invoked: engine and factory can never skew apart.
        run: |
          # The stub passes the same literal its uses-line pins — engine and
          # factory can never skew apart. Keep both in sync when flipping refs.
          echo "FACTORY_REF=${{ inputs.factory_ref }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: "Checkout factory (dmtools-agents: runners + scripts)"
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          repository: IstiN/dmtools-agents
          ref: ${{ env.FACTORY_REF }}
          path: factory-agents
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Export fa session identity + cache keys
        env:
          AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.config }}
          AI_TEAMMATE_DISPLAY_KEY: GH-${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
          AI_TEAMMATE_CONCURRENCY_KEY: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
        run: bash factory-agents/setup/cache.sh keys fa-session

      - name: Restore fa session (resume the ticket conversation)
        # actions/cache saves are denied on issues-event runs (job token is
        # cache-read-only there), so the session tree rides a dedicated git
        # branch per issue; the per-issue concurrency group serializes writers.
        env:
          FA_SESS_BRANCH: fa-sess/${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
        run: |
          if git fetch --depth 1 origin "refs/heads/$FA_SESS_BRANCH"; then
            git checkout "refs/remotes/origin/$FA_SESS_BRANCH" -- .dmtools/fa-sessions
            # Unstage (checkout <ref> -- <path> STAGES): the session store
            # belongs on the fa-sess branch only.
            git restore --staged .dmtools/fa-sessions
            echo "→ fa session restored from $FA_SESS_BRANCH"
          else
            echo "→ no saved fa session yet ($FA_SESS_BRANCH absent) — starting fresh"
          fi

      - name: Cache fa CLI (by version)
        if: env.FA_VERSION != 'latest'
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.local/bin/fa
            ~/lib
          key: fa-${{ env.FA_VERSION }}-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' (or empty) resolves to the current release tag so the
        # version-locked install.sh URL keeps working; owner mandate
        # 2026-10-01: machine legs always track the latest CLI/agents.
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION:-}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Cache dmtools CLI (by version)
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.dmtools/bin
          key: dmtools-${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION }}-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}

      - name: "Install prerequisites (fa; no-op on cache hit)"
        # Authenticated gh api download first — anonymous release-asset
        # downloads hit GitHub edge caches that served stale 404s for hours
        # after a re-cut release (observed 2026-09-12).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if ! command -v fa >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ ! -x "${HOME}/.local/bin/fa" ]; then
            case "$(uname -m)" in
              x86_64) FA_ARCH="x64" ;;
              *)      FA_ARCH="arm64" ;;
            esac
            tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
            # 'latest' is a WORD, not a tag — gh release download takes a
            # literal tag; with no tag it resolves the latest release.
            # (Live failure on IstiN/flutter_agent_harness gh-623: the repo
            # has no FA_VERSION var -> 'latest' -> "release not found".)
            # A fresh latest release can also be asset-less for a while
            # (v0.1.418 2026-09-18: tag landed, binaries never uploaded ->
            # review leg died "no assets to download"). Walk back to the
            # newest release that actually ships the CLI bundle.
            if [ "${FA_VERSION}" = "latest" ] || [ -z "${FA_VERSION}" ]; then
              for t in $(gh release list \
                  --repo IstiN/flutter_agent_harness --limit 10 \
                  --json tagName --jq '.[].tagName'); do
                if gh release view "$t" --repo IstiN/flutter_agent_harness \
                    --json assets --jq '.assets[].name' 2>/dev/null \
                    | grep -q "^fa-linux-${FA_ARCH}\.tar\.gz$"; then
                  FA_VERSION="$t"
                  echo "fa install: latest asset-less, falling back to ${FA_VERSION}"
                  break
                fi
              done
            fi
            gh release download "${FA_VERSION}" \
              --repo IstiN/flutter_agent_harness \
              --pattern "fa-linux-${FA_ARCH}.tar.gz" --dir "${tmp}" --clobber
            tar -xzf "${tmp}/fa-linux-${FA_ARCH}.tar.gz" -C "${tmp}"
            mkdir -p "${HOME}/.local/bin" "${HOME}/.local/lib"
            cp "${tmp}/bundle/bin/fa" "${HOME}/.local/bin/fa"
            chmod +x "${HOME}/.local/bin/fa"
            cp -R "${tmp}/bundle/lib/." "${HOME}/.local/lib/" 2>/dev/null || true
          fi
          bash factory-agents/setup/install.sh "fa:${FA_VERSION}"

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        # The installer ships as a release asset, version-locked to the
        # bundle it installs — no copy of install.sh in the target repo.
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      # flutter-action treats a literal version string strictly — the words
      # stable/beta/main/master are CHANNELS and crash the action ("Unable
      # to determine Flutter version for channel: stable", live: gh-623 run
      # 35370007049). Two steps with plain if-comparisons — the GH parser
      # rejects map-indexing expressions inside with:.
      - name: Set up Flutter for agent work (channel)
        if: inputs.flutter-version == 'stable' || inputs.flutter-version == 'beta' || inputs.flutter-version == 'main' || inputs.flutter-version == 'master'
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          channel: ${{ inputs.flutter-version }}
          cache: true

      - name: Set up Flutter for agent work (pinned version)
        if: inputs.flutter-version != '' && !(inputs.flutter-version == 'stable' || inputs.flutter-version == 'beta' || inputs.flutter-version == 'main' || inputs.flutter-version == 'master')
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          flutter-version: ${{ inputs.flutter-version }}
          cache: true

      - name: Verify prerequisites
        run: |
          fa --version
          dmtools --version
          if [ -n "${{ inputs.flutter-version }}" ]; then
            flutter --version
            dart --version
          fi

      - name: Configure Git Author + push credentials
        # Purge the checkout's App token and make SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN the
        # credential that wins for github.com pushes (all logic in the
        # shared installer — one copy serves every push path in the job).
        env:
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash factory-agents/setup/install-source-git-credentials.sh

      - name: Trace git credential stack (push-time evidence)
        # gh-63 Task 1 — same run that pushes, right before the agent.
        # What each section proves:
        #   --show-origin        WHERE each credential source lives; the
        #                        extraheader section must come back empty —
        #                        asserted below, so any resurrection of the
        #                        App-token header (checkout layout change,
        #                        mid-run config write) fails the run here
        #                        instead of silently re-arming bot pushes
        #   submodule foreach    same proof for each submodule local config
        #                        (checkout arms those with submodules: true)
        #   git credential fill  dry-runs the exact push-path resolution and
        #                        shows the winning username; the password is
        #                        masked, and the helper's stderr line confirms
        #                        SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN served the credential
        env:
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p .dmtools
          echo "── credential.helper — all scopes, with origins ──"
          git config --show-origin --get-all credential.helper || true
          git config --show-origin --get-all credential.https://github.com.helper || true
          echo "── http.https://github.com/.extraheader (must be empty — App token purged) ──"
          # Redact the VALUE (gh-63 review threads 11/12): on a leftover this
          # dump prints AUTHORIZATION: basic <base64(App token)> — GitHub's
          # log masking matches the raw token string, not its base64 form.
          # git 2.x prints "<origin>\t<value>" (--show-origin --get-all has
          # NO key= prefix), so redact everything after the first TAB — a
          # sed on '=' alone would only trim the base64 padding. The origin
          # (file/scope) stays visible; a tab-less line is fully redacted.
          git config --show-origin --get-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader | sed -E 's/^([^\t]*\t).*/\1<redacted>/; t; s/.+/<redacted> (unexpected line without origin)/' || true
          if git config --get-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader | grep -q .; then
            echo "::error::App-token extraheader still present after purge — pushes would authenticate as github-actions[bot]"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "── submodule extraheaders (must be empty — App token purged there too) ──"
          # checkout arms every submodule's local config with the same token;
          # a push made from inside agents/ must not fall back to it (gh-63).
          # The probe echoes a LEFTOVER marker line only when a config is
          # still armed, so "no submodules" and "all clean" stay quiet.
          # The marker names the submodule but NEVER the header value: it is
          # AUTHORIZATION: basic <base64(App token)>, decodable and NOT masked
          # by GitHub log redaction (gh-63 review threads 11/12).
          sub_leftovers="$(git submodule foreach --quiet --recursive \
            'c="$(git config --get-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader || true)"; [ -z "$c" ] || echo "LEFTOVER ${sm_path}: <redacted>"' \
            || true)"
          if [ -n "$sub_leftovers" ]; then
            echo "::error::App-token extraheader still present in a submodule config after purge — pushes from inside the submodule would authenticate as github-actions[bot]"
            printf '%s\n' "$sub_leftovers"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "── commit identity ──"
          git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT
          git var GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT
          echo "── dry-run: credential a github.com push would use ──"
          # Capture first, then assert: with GIT_ASKPASS=echo `git credential
          # fill` exits 0 even when NO helper answered (echo prints its prompt
          # back, git accepts it as a bogus credential) — only the
          # SOURCE helper's username proves the SOURCE credential wins.
          # CRED_HELPER_CONTEXT tags the helper's log line so this dry-run
          # stays distinguishable from real pushes in the evidence log.
          out="$(printf 'protocol=https\nhost=github.com\n' | CRED_HELPER_CONTEXT=trace-dry-run GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 GIT_ASKPASS=echo git credential fill 2>&1)" || true
          if printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '^username=x-access-token$'; then
            echo "$out" | sed -E 's/^password=.+/password=<redacted — served by the SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN helper>/'
          else
            echo "::error::dry-run credential was NOT served by the SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN helper — a github.com push would not authenticate as the SOURCE account"
            printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -E 's/^password=.+/password=<redacted>/'
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Seed local git excludes (factory workspace artifacts)
        # Everything the factory/agent scribbles into the workspace that must
        # NEVER reach a commit (agents run `git add -A`). .git/info/exclude is
        # local-only by construction — no .gitignore pollution in agent PRs.
        run: |
          {
            echo '# factory workspace artifacts (seeded per-run, never commit)'
            echo '.codegraph/'
            echo '.dmtools/fa-trace.log'
            echo '.dmtools/run-output.txt'
            echo '.dmtools/stall-capture.log'
            echo '.dmtools/fa-sessions/'
            echo '.dmtools/copilot-sessions/'
            echo '.fah/bash_jobs/'
            echo '# the factory clone itself: an in-index gitlink without'
            echo '# .gitmodules breaks every actions/checkout with submodules'
            echo 'factory-agents/'
          } >> .git/info/exclude

      - name: Write the issue into the agent input folder
        if: inputs.pr == ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
        run: |
          # ticket.json carries the tracker-contract fields: dmtools hydrates
          # it into params.ticket for every JS action (Tracker abstraction).
          mkdir -p "input/gh-${NUMBER}"
          gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --json number,title,body,url,state,labels \
            -q '{key: ("gh-" + (.number|tostring)), number: .number,
                 title: .title, body: .body, url: .url, state: .state,
                 labels: [.labels[].name]}' \
            > "input/gh-${NUMBER}/ticket.json"
          gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --json title,body -q '.title, .body' > input/ticket.md
          echo "input/ticket.md: $(wc -l < input/ticket.md) lines"

      - name: Write the PR into the agent input folder (PR-anchored runs)
        # #687: the PR is the anchor — the pr-N contextId is what the agent
        # scripts key on; ticket.json carries the same tracker-contract
        # shape so hydration paths stay uniform.
        if: inputs.pr != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ inputs.pr }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p "input/pr-${PR_NUMBER}"
          gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --json number,title,body,url,state,labels \
            -q '{key: ("pr-" + (.number|tostring)), number: .number,
                 title: .title, body: .body, url: .url, state: .state,
                 labels: [.labels[].name]}' \
            > "input/pr-${PR_NUMBER}/ticket.json"
          gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --json title,body -q '.title, .body' > input/ticket.md
          echo "input/ticket.md: $(wc -l < input/ticket.md) lines"

      - name: Mark machine job started (issue task list)
        # Deterministic start marker in the issue body — survives agent
        # crashes/timeouts because the DONE twin below runs on always().
        # Contract: a "## Machine jobs" section with one task-list line per
        # factory run; the line's run URL is the unique id used to flip it.
        # PR-anchored runs skip it: no issue body to carry the task list.
        if: inputs.pr == ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
          JOB_LEG: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.kind }}
          RUNNER: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.runner }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          repo="${{ github.repository }}"
          leg="${JOB_LEG:-dev} ($(basename "${RUNNER:-agent}" .json))"
          line="- [ ] ▶ ${leg} · [run](${RUN_URL}) · started $(date -u '+%H:%M') ⏳"
          gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --json body -q .body > /tmp/issue_body.md
          # Collapse trailing blank lines first: body rewrites (jq raw
          # output, earlier appends, agent edits) can leave trailing
          # newlines, and a marker appended after them splits the GitHub
          # task list into separate lists (broken formatting). "$(cat …)"
          # strips ALL trailing newlines; printf adds exactly one back.
          printf '%s\n' "$(cat /tmp/issue_body.md)" > /tmp/issue_body.md
          if grep -q '^## Machine jobs' /tmp/issue_body.md; then
            printf '%s\n' "$line" >> /tmp/issue_body.md
          else
            printf '\n## Machine jobs\n%s\n' "$line" >> /tmp/issue_body.md
          fi
          gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --body-file /tmp/issue_body.md
          echo "job marker added: $line"

      - name: Run agent (fa provider via runner env overrides)
        id: run_agent
        # Hard cap under the job's 260 min: a hung agent session must FAIL
        # the leg (the always() post-actions then run inside the remaining
        # budget and the red path re-queues) instead of the job-level
        # timeout killing everything mid-post-action. NOT 45: a real fix is
        # a 40-80 minute session (gh-623 was killed mid-work at exactly 61).
        # NOT 110: dev legs over Flutter sources run the analyzer + the
        # full flutter test suite — fa gh-1077 was killed mid-work at
        # exactly 110 (live flutter_tester orphans at teardown, PR step
        # never reached) — 2026-09-30.
        timeout-minutes: 240
        env:
          CI_RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          RUNNER: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.runner }}
          AI_AGENT_PROVIDER: fa
          AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.config }}
          AI_TEAMMATE_DISPLAY_KEY: GH-${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
          AI_TEAMMATE_CONCURRENCY_KEY: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
          ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
          KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # Agent-pack registry base (dm.ai #579): runners may parent packs
          # by REGISTRY ref (`pr_review@latest`) — the resolver reads the
          # releases base (incl. catalog.json) from this env. Callers set
          # the repo VARIABLE to their pinned dmtools-agents release tag;
          # unset (or empty) keeps the previous file-only behavior and the
          # resolver fails with an explicit "no pack registry" error.
          DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY }}
          # gh operations inside the session must act AS the SOURCE account:
          # events created with GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger workflows.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || github.token }}
        run: |
          # #542 mechanical guard: interpose the git push/commit guard shim at
          # the FRONT of PATH before `dmtools run` so EVERY push path in the
          # session is covered — both the fa agent's own shell tool (inherits
          # the dmtools process env) and the JS pre/post-actions'
          # cli_execute_command (PATH-resolved `git`). Refuses pushes to
          # main/master/default branch and closing keywords in commit
          # messages. Deliberately NOT written to $GITHUB_PATH: later workflow
          # steps (session-branch persistence) push legitimately.
          GIT_GUARD_BIN="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/git-push-guard-bin"
          mkdir -p "${GIT_GUARD_BIN}"
          ln -sf "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/factory-agents/scripts/git-push-guard.sh" "${GIT_GUARD_BIN}/git"
          export PATH="${GIT_GUARD_BIN}:${PATH}"
          git --version  # resolves through the shim — proves the wiring
          # FULL session trace: FA_LOG_FILE tees every line fa prints to the
          # file, uploaded as an artifact below; dmtools mirrors child output
          # live to its own stderr, so the agent's work streams into the log.
          FA_LOG_FILE="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.dmtools/fa-trace.log"
          export FA_LOG_FILE
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "${FA_LOG_FILE}")"
          touch "${FA_LOG_FILE}"
          echo "fa full trace: ${FA_LOG_FILE}"
          # ── dmtools self-heal (self-hosted runners keep a persistent $HOME) ──
          # A stale or half-updated ~/.dmtools/bin from an older install
          # layout kills the leg instantly with "Error: Cannot open file"
          # (live: epam/dmtools-dart pr-301 review, run 36614989141 — the
          # install step's own `dmtools --version` printed 0.1.22, and the
          # run step 14s later died before any output). Probe what PATH
          # actually resolves at RUN time, verify it, and force-reinstall
          # the pinned bundle when the resolution is broken.
          echo "── dmtools self-check ──"
          echo "resolved: $(command -v dmtools || echo MISSING)"
          ls -la "${HOME}/.dmtools/bin" 2>/dev/null | head -8 || true
          if ! dmtools --version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "dmtools on PATH is broken — force reinstall (${DMTOOLS_VERSION})"
            curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
              -o /tmp/dmtools-heal.sh
            bash /tmp/dmtools-heal.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
            export PATH="${HOME}/.dmtools/bin:${PATH}"
            hash -r
          fi
          echo "resolved after heal: $(command -v dmtools || echo MISSING)"
          dmtools --version
          RUN_OUTPUT="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.dmtools/run-output.txt"
          # #687: machine login rides jobParams so PR-anchored verdicts arm
          # the merge pipeline regardless of what the checked-out branch's
          # .dmtools/config.js carries (postPRReviewComments reads
          # jobParams.machineAuthor first).
          DMTOOLS_ARGS=()
          MA='${{ inputs.machine-author }}'
          if [ -n "$MA" ]; then
            DMTOOLS_ARGS+=('{"params":{"jobParams":{"machineAuthor":"'"$MA"'"}}}')
          fi
          # fa-trace staleness watchdog: the fa session streams EVERY turn
          # and tool call into FA_LOG_FILE, so a healthy leg touches it
          # constantly. If the file goes quiet mid-run the session is
          # brain-dead (live: dmd PR-266 legs — process alive, dmtools
          # timer ticking, fa trace silent from the first minute, step
          # in_progress forever). Without this the leg ZOMBIES: nothing
          # fails, no verdict is produced, the SM never re-queues. On
          # staleness: marker into run-output (post-actions + artifacts
          # carry it, so the failure is diagnosable, not silent), then
          # kill dmtools — its non-zero exit fails the step and the
          # standard red path takes over. FA_TRACE_STALE_MINUTES defaults
          # to 10 (healthy legs write every few seconds; ten quiet minutes
          # is unambiguous). Tunable per repo via a workflow env if a
          # provider ever proves slower.
          (
            stale_limit="${FA_TRACE_STALE_MINUTES:-10}"
            while sleep 60; do
              [ -f "${FA_LOG_FILE}" ] || continue
              mtime="$(stat -c %Y "${FA_LOG_FILE}" 2>/dev/null || stat -f %m "${FA_LOG_FILE}" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
              [ "${mtime}" != "0" ] || continue
              age_min=$(( ( $(date +%s) - mtime ) / 60 ))
              if [ "${age_min}" -ge "${stale_limit}" ]; then
                {
                  echo ""
                  echo "🛑 FA-TRACE-STALE-WATCHDOG: no agent output for ${age_min} min" \
                       "(limit ${stale_limit}) at $(date -u +%FT%TZ) — the agent session is presumed hung."
                  echo "FA-TRACE-STALE-WATCHDOG=1 (diagnose via the fa-trace artifact; the leg fails and the SM red path re-queues)"
                } | tee -a "${RUN_OUTPUT}"
                echo "::error::fa-trace stale for ${age_min} min (limit ${stale_limit}) — agent session presumed hung; failing the leg"
                # Best-effort kill: dmtools first (its death non-zeros the
                # step), then the orphaned fa provider child.
                pkill -f "dmtools run" 2>/dev/null || true
                pkill -f "fa --session" 2>/dev/null || true
                exit 0
              fi
            done
          ) &
          WATCHDOG_PID=$!
          # Stall-capture sidecar (dmd PR-266 hang investigation 2026-09-28):
          # the Bitrise-pool probe never catches the workload stall because
          # it runs on an IDLE VM; this monitor rides the agent run itself.
          # Every 20s: load, PSI io/mem, all D-state processes, and for every
          # live git/sh/dart process the kernel wait channel (/proc wchan)
          # plus stack and open fds — wchan names WHAT the process sleeps on
          # (disk I/O, network, futex, pipe) which is the proof either way.
          STALL_LOG="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.dmtools/stall-capture.log"
          : > "${STALL_LOG}"
          (
            while sleep 20; do
              {
                echo "=== $(date -u +%H:%M:%S) load=$(cut -d' ' -f1 /proc/loadavg)"
                sed 's/^/psi_io  /' /proc/pressure/io 2>/dev/null
                sed 's/^/psi_mem /' /proc/pressure/memory 2>/dev/null
                ps -eo pid,ppid,state,etime,wchan:32,comm | awk 'NR==1 || $3 ~ /^D/'
                # fa/dmtools comm names do not always match pgrep -x patterns
                # (AOT binary renames, wrapper shells) — match the cmdline.
                for p in $(pgrep -x git 2>/dev/null) $(pgrep -f "bin/fa" 2>/dev/null) $(pgrep -f "dmtools run" 2>/dev/null); do
                  echo "--- pid $p ($(cat /proc/$p/comm 2>/dev/null)) state=$(awk '{print $3}' /proc/$p/stat 2>/dev/null) wchan=$(cat /proc/$p/wchan 2>/dev/null)"
                  echo "    syscall: $(cat /proc/$p/syscall 2>/dev/null)"
                  echo "    cmdline: $(tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/$p/cmdline 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-200)"
                  ls -l /proc/$p/fd 2>/dev/null | awk '{print "    fd:", $9, $10, $11}' | head -12
                  cat /proc/$p/stack 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/    stack: /'
                done
              } >> "${STALL_LOG}" 2>&1
            done
          ) &
          STALL_MON_PID=$!
          trap 'kill "${WATCHDOG_PID}" "${STALL_MON_PID}" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
          dmtools run "${RUNNER}" ${DMTOOLS_ARGS[@]+"${DMTOOLS_ARGS[@]}"} \
            --metadata '{"contextId":"${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}"}' \
            --ciRunUrl "${CI_RUN_URL}" --debug 2>&1 | tee "${RUN_OUTPUT}"

        if: always() && inputs.pr == ''

blocks.text:
# PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file carries
# only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository event
# triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]  # dev leg; review/rework ride labels too
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  dedupe:
    # First-wins: the `issues` trigger fires on assigned AND labeled, so one
    # manual launch can dispatch two dev legs minutes apart (live gh-305 twin,
    # 2026-09-30: 36767724353 in_progress + 36767943650 pending behind the
    # concurrency group, both event=issues). The concurrency group only
    # SERIALIZES twins — this gate makes the younger run self-cancel when an
    # older live run of this workflow already anchors the same issue/pr.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      duplicate: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.duplicate }}
    steps:
      - name: Self-cancel if an identical live leg already holds the anchor
        id: gate
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          ANCHOR: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
        run: |
          case "$ANCHOR" in
            pr-*) T="$ANCHOR" ;;
            *)    T="gh-$ANCHOR" ;;
          esac
          LIVE=$( { gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status in_progress --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                    gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status queued    --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                    gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status pending   --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                  } | jq -s --argjson self '${{ github.run_id }}' --arg t "$T" '
                    [ .[]
                      | select(.databaseId != $self)
                      | select(.displayTitle | test("(^|[^0-9])" + $t + "([^0-9]|$)")) ]
                    | length')
          if [ "${LIVE:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::notice::identical live leg holds $T — cancelling this duplicate ($LIVE holder(s) found)"
            echo "duplicate=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            gh run cancel "${{ github.run_id }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" || true
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "duplicate=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  factory:
    needs: dedupe
    if: needs.dedupe.outputs.duplicate != 'true'
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA the `agents` submodule pins — a branch
    # ref executes the branch head at run start, and the head has since
    # renamed the reusable workflows away from factory/<name>.yml. This
    # commit has the called paths and the self-pin that checks out
    # factory-agents/ at the same SHA. Flip in lockstep with the
    # submodule when dmtools-agents#424 merges (bump the submodule,
    # then repoint this ref at the new SHA).
    # Guarded by test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@b93dc51c1030839153c9bb86c8aa2e6b3fad82de
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: 210e8ac5efa06db24a249f174d12f98aadbcb9ab
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'stub' }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}
# DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY (pack registry base) is read by the factory from
# this repo's VARIABLE of the same name — see dmtools-agents#574.

blocks.text:
# Factory Merge Trigger — the canonical pr_approved merge bot.
#
# One reusable implementation for every factory repo. The calling repo
# keeps a thin stub that declares the EVENT triggers (workflow_run on its
# CI workflow, optionally issues:labeled) and calls this one — `on:` in a
# stub cannot be parameterized, everything below the event boundary is
# shared here.
#
# The tracker is the CALLING repo's GitHub issues (no Jira, no external
# services):
#
#   issue labeled `pr_approved` → linked PR found → required checks green
#   (branch protection is the gate: mergeStateStatus CLEAN) → squash-merge
#   → label removed → comment posted on the issue.
#
# Linking conventions (any of):
#   - PR body contains `Closes #NN` / `Fixes #NN` / `Resolves #NN`
#   - PR branch name starts with `NN-` (e.g. `42-fix-foo`)
#   - PR branch name matches `gh-0*NN` (the gh-N display-title convention)
#   - the PR itself carries the label (pr_review approves via
#     scm.addLabel) — mapped back to its linked issue
#
# Prerequisites (in the calling repo):
#   vars: MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED (fuse — the job skips itself until `true`)
#   branch protection on main with required checks + strict (the machine
#   only merges CLEAN PRs, so protection defines what "ready" means).
#   github.token is sufficient for everything; pass a PAT via
#   secrets: inherit if the caller needs one (see GH_TOKEN below).

name: Factory Merge Trigger

run-name: 'Merge Trigger : CI passed → merge pr_approved issues'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runs-on label for the merge job'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      remove_pr_label:
        description: 'Also remove pr_approved from the merged PR (dmd convention)'
        type: boolean
        default: true
      map_pr_labels:
        description: 'Map PRs labeled pr_approved back to their linked issues'
        type: boolean
        default: true
      gh_branch_pattern:
        description: 'Also link via branch names like gh-0*NN'
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: read

jobs:
  merge-trigger:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # Same-repo guard: PRs from forks must not trigger merges. The
    # issues:labeled entry path (dmd) re-enters without a workflow_run.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' && github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_run' &&
       github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
       github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository)
    concurrency:
      group: merge-trigger-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.event.issue.number }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
      - name: Gate on MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED
        id: gate
        env:
          ENABLED: ${{ vars.MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED }}
        run: |
          if [ "$ENABLED" = "true" ]; then
            echo "enabled=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "enabled=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::merge-trigger scaffold is wired but disabled — set the MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED repo variable to true (after branch protection + required checks are in place)."
          fi

      - name: Merge issues labeled pr_approved
        if: steps.gate.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PAT_TOKEN || github.token }}
          LABEL: pr_approved
          CI_RUN_URL: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.html_url }}
          REMOVE_PR_LABEL: ${{ inputs.remove_pr_label }}
          MAP_PR_LABELS: ${{ inputs.map_pr_labels }}
          GH_BRANCH_PATTERN: ${{ inputs.gh_branch_pattern }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          repo="${{ github.repository }}"
          # Candidates come from BOTH sides: the issue label (human/bot)
          # and the PR label (pr_review approves via scm.addLabel on the
          # PR) — map PR labels back to their linked issues.
          issues=$(gh issue list --repo "$repo" --label "$LABEL" --state open \
            --json number --jq '.[].number')
          if [ "$MAP_PR_LABELS" = "true" ]; then
            prs_labeled=$(gh pr list --repo "$repo" --label "$LABEL" --state open \
              --json number,body,headRefName --jq '.[] | "\(.number)\t\(.body // "")\t\(.headRefName)"')
            while IFS=$'\t' read -r prn body branch; do
              [ -n "$prn" ] || continue
              n=$(echo "$body" | grep -oiE '\b(closes|fixes|resolves)\s+#[0-9]+' | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || true)
              [ -n "$n" ] || n=$(echo "$branch" | grep -oE '^[0-9]+' || true)
              [ -n "$n" ] || n=$(echo "$branch" | grep -oE 'gh-[0-9]+' | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || true)
              if [ -n "$n" ]; then
                open=$(gh issue view "$n" --repo "$repo" --json state --jq .state 2>/dev/null || true)
                [ "$open" = "OPEN" ] && issues="$issues $n"
              fi
            done < <(printf '%s\n' "$prs_labeled")
            issues=$(echo $issues | tr ' ' '\n' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
          fi
          if [ -z "${issues// /}" ]; then
            echo "no issues labeled '$LABEL' — nothing to merge"
            exit 0
          fi
          merged=0; skipped=0
          for n in $issues; do
            echo "::group::issue #$n"
            gh_pat='(?i)\\b(closes|fixes|resolves)\\s+#'"$n"'\\b'
            branch_pat='^'"$n"'[-_.]'
            if [ "$GH_BRANCH_PATTERN" = "true" ]; then
              link_sel="((.body // \"\") | test(\"$gh_pat\")) or (.headRefName | test(\"$branch_pat\")) or (.headRefName | test(\"(^|[-_./])gh-0*$n$\"))"
            else
              link_sel="((.body // \"\") | test(\"$gh_pat\")) or (.headRefName | test(\"$branch_pat\"))"
            fi
            pr=$(gh pr list --repo "$repo" --state open \
              --json number,body,headRefName \
              --jq "[.[] | select($link_sel) | .number] | first // empty")
            if [ -z "$pr" ]; then
              echo "issue #$n: no linked open PR (add 'Closes #$n' to the PR body or name the branch '$n-…') — skipping"
              skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "::endgroup::"; continue
            fi
            state=$(gh pr view "$pr" --repo "$repo" \
              --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus \
              --jq '.mergeable + ":" + .mergeStateStatus')
            echo "linked PR #$pr — $state"
            case "$state" in
              MERGEABLE:CLEAN)
                if err=$(gh pr merge "$pr" --repo "$repo" --squash 2>&1); then
                  merged=$((merged+1))
                  gh issue edit "$n" --repo "$repo" --remove-label "$LABEL" || true
                  if [ "$REMOVE_PR_LABEL" = "true" ]; then
                    gh pr edit "$pr" --repo "$repo" --remove-label "$LABEL" || true
                  fi
                  gh issue comment "$n" --repo "$repo" \
                    --body "🔀 Merged #$pr (CI: ${CI_RUN_URL:-run})" || true
                  echo "✅ merged #$pr for issue #$n"
                else
                  skipped=$((skipped+1))
                  echo "❌ merge of #$pr failed: $err"
                fi
                ;;
              MERGEABLE:BEHIND)
                skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "⏳ behind main — the SM (silent-update-behind) refreshes it, then re-dispatches CI"
                ;;
              MERGEABLE:BLOCKED|MERGEABLE:UNSTABLE)
                skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "⏳ required checks not green yet"
                ;;
              *)
                skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "⛔ not mergeable ($state) — needs manual attention"
                ;;
            esac
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done
          echo "summary: merged=$merged skipped=$skipped"
